# Historical-error-weighted NIFTY inputs

Design frozen before this extension's model results were inspected. The first
17 November forecast stays unchanged. This extension learns feature coefficients
and learns group weights from earlier predictions' realized errors.

## Information and evaluation boundaries

Reuse the hashed price freezes, completed-session labels and conservative global
clock from the first experiment. Add separately frozen Upstox institutional
history, available only since April 2026, using overlapping 35-calendar-day
anchor requests plus the saved current window because the endpoint returns at
most 30 trading days. Actual returned session dates govern joins; the observed
windows end around the requested anchor despite its documented start-date name.
For a historical
decision after the preceding Indian session, institutional EOD values are assumed
available by 00:30 IST. Publication times/vintage revisions are not reconstructed;
this assumption is disclosed. No absolute cash amount is interpreted as crore.
Use (buy-sell)/(buy+sell), which cancels a common positive unit scale.

The latest 504 target sessions are a fixed outer evaluation, with the latest 126
also reported separately. Earlier history supplies model fitting and historical
predictions for learning weights. All fitted weights at a target use only labels
resolved by its preceding decision day. The outer period was already inspected
in the earlier study: this is exploratory reuse, not an untouched confirmatory
holdout. The next session outcome is still forward and unresolved.

## Two learned layers and probability calibration

1. Partition features into disjoint, interpretable groups: trend, short-term
   price, candle shape/gaps, volatility, banks/financials, other sectors,
   participation, global equities, oil/currency, GIFT Nifty, institutional cash,
   and FII derivative positioning. Each group's L2 logistic expert learns signed
   standardized input coefficients. Monthly refits use at most 1,260 completed
   targets, exponential recency weights with a 252-session half-life, and fixed
   L2 penalty 25. At least 252 observed training rows are required for established
   groups, 63 for the separate short-history institutional experts. Availability
   requires at least half of a group's raw features; imputation and scaling are
   fitted only on eligible training rows. Missingness flags are explicit.
2. Retain each expert's genuinely chronological out-of-sample predictions. At
   every next decision, fit nonnegative blend weights summing to one by minimizing
   recency-weighted Brier loss over the last 504 resolved predictions. Meta-loss
   half-life is 126 sessions. Include a neutral 50% expert. A fixed 0.005 squared
   penalty toward the neutral expert limits fragile concentration. A group needs
   at least 126 prior out-of-sample predictions, adequate current inputs, and at
   least 252 observed training rows before it can enter the primary blend.
   Experts with shorter history are recorded and scored in shadow, with zero
   primary allocation; zero here means insufficient evidence, not irrelevance.
3. The primary forecast is that adaptive blend passed through a monotone logistic
   calibrator fitted only to its preceding 252 chronological forecasts, with at
   least 126 examples. Fit an intercept and a nonnegative slope (maximum 3), with
   fixed penalty 10 toward intercept 0 and slope 1. A weighted-Brier adaptive
   blend and an equal-group blend are retained as controls; there is no result-
   based winner selection. Report the neutral 50/50 and prior experiment controls.

No parameter grid or performance-triggered replacement of this design. Preserve
monthly expert fits, daily group allocations, per-feature signed coefficients,
raw and calibrated forecasts, source hashes, all candidate scores and group
eligibility reasons. Expert intercepts and missingness effects are not invented
as named raw input weights. Group percentages are actual probability-blend
allocations; per-feature logistic coefficients act inside those groups. These
are distinct quantities and neither is a causal effect.

## Scoring and forward use

Report Brier loss, log loss, accuracy, calibration bins, first/second halves,
latest 126 sessions, neutral/frequency controls and 2,000 ten-session-block paired
intervals. Include the 503-session subset excluding Monday's provisional target.
Produce daily allocation and cumulative loss charts. Run targeted leakage tests
by changing future labels and inputs and confirming earlier weights are identical.

Save a new immutable, dated forecast rather than editing the first call. The
existing outcome scorer can evaluate this forecast in its own directory. Future
reruns learn new weights only after new outcomes have resolved. This is a local
research workflow, not an unattended watcher or a scheduled automation.

# Five-session and twenty-one-session forecast experiment

Retain the user's strict two-year input boundary: 17 November 2024 through
16 November 2026, with no older indicator initialization. Reuse the earlier
frozen price context and separately saved institutional history. Forecast from
the 16 November 2026 close for the next 5 observed NSE trading sessions (week)
and 21 sessions (month). Expected endpoint dates use a separately frozen current
Upstox NSE calendar, corroborated by the official NSE 2026 holiday circular.
Trading-session count is the outcome definition if the future calendar changes.

## Targets and when an answer becomes available

For a decision after session t's close, label the return C[t+h]/C[t]-1, h=5 or
21. A training, weighting or calibration row is eligible only if its endpoint
session has closed by the decision. Merely being an earlier forecast origin is
not sufficient. Fit horizon-specific coefficients, group allocations and
calibrators. Do not compound or stretch the daily forecast.

Use the same 71 features, 12 disjoint groups, fixed logistic penalty 25,
252-session expert recency half-life, 126-session meta half-life, 0.005 neutral
shrinkage, and monotone calibrator penalty 10. No parameter search. Historical
experts refit monthly, with the current call freshly fitted. Established groups
need 252 matured training labels; short-history institutional experts need 63
for shadow predictions and 252 plus 126 matured OOS errors for primary use.
The first expert decision starts after 252+h-1 feature rows, allowing 252
matured h-session labels. Primary weighting and calibration each require 126
earlier, fully matured out-of-sample outcomes. All these thresholds count
overlapping rows, not independent weeks/months; disclose that limitation.

## Return magnitudes and ranges

At each decision retain up to the latest 252 matured horizon returns. Separate
their positive and nonpositive observations, allocating total probability p
to the positive sample and 1-p to the nonpositive sample, where p is the
predeclared calibrated adaptive sign estimate. Inside each subset distribute
mass equally. Report mixture median/mean, central 50% and 80% quantiles and
corresponding index levels. This assumes historical conditional move sizes
persist; it is not a separately fitted return regressor or a guaranteed range.
Also retain unconditional empirical reference quantiles and score median MAE
and interval coverage chronologically. Never use unfinished h-session returns
for a current magnitude distribution.

## Honest evaluation of overlapping outcomes

Report all post-training forecasts and separately those with fully learned
weights/calibration, selected by evidence availability, not performance.
Compare neutral 50/50, rolling matured-label frequency, equal eligible groups,
raw adaptive weights and the predeclared calibrated primary on identical dates.
Include always-up/always-down direction accuracies and an unconditional median
return control. Count a greedily selected non-overlapping evaluation subset
whose next origin is no earlier than the previous endpoint. Score it separately.

Use 2,000 paired moving-block resamples with block length 2*h, only when at
least 8*h evaluated origin rows exist. Otherwise omit the interval and report
insufficient independent history. Do not use daily ten-session blocks for
21-session targets or label overlapping monthly forecasts independent tests.
Report published-only subsets excluding targets whose endpoint uses Monday's
provisional quote. This is exploratory reuse of the same historical period.

## Forward record

Freeze separate week/month outcomes, endpoint dates, horizon-native levels,
probabilities, weights, inputs/code hashes and unresolved outcome fields. A
manual scorer may write a separate outcome artifact once each horizon has
enough published daily candles. Preserve all earlier daily and two-year calls.
No unattended watcher, scheduled automation or orders are part of this request.

# NIFTY session direction experiment

Frozen design for the 17 November 2026 pre-market experiment. This is a
prediction study of the cash index, with no orders or option profit claims.

## Questions and information cutoff

Primary: will the official NIFTY daily close exceed the preceding session's
official close? Secondary: will the close exceed today's opening level?
These are separate labels. A positive overnight gap need not mean a positive
open-to-close session. Also estimate the distribution of closing returns.

Freeze raw inputs with acquisition times and hashes. Use only completed Indian
sessions before the forecast date. Daily bar timestamps identify sessions, not
their publication times. Historical reconstruction assumes a completed bar was
available by the next session; it is not a vintage or broker-latency replay.
Today's global partial-session quotes are commentary inputs, not historical
final-close features. Undated or stale options are disclosed, never treated as
fresh. Preserve the complete dashboard catalog, including unavailable concepts
(127 concepts in the current catalog).

## Fixed candidates (no parameter search)

1. Rolling unconditional upward frequency (the main probability baseline).
2. Previous-day direction and 20-session trend (simple directional baselines).
3. L2 logistic regression on NIFTY's own completed price features.
4. L2 logistic regression with sector leadership, breadth, India VIX and the
   latest safely completed global daily sessions (if the provider supplies history).
5. Distance-weighted 60-nearest historical analogues using the same context.
6. Nonlinear logistic regression using 64 fixed random Fourier features.
7. Equal-weight ensemble of candidates 4, 5 and 6, fixed before evaluation.

Use the most recent 504 eligible completed target sessions for chronological
walk-forward evaluation, at least 504 training examples and at most the
preceding 1,260. Refit on each target calendar month. At a refit all training
labels must already be resolved before that month's first decision. Scaling,
imputation and all fitted coefficients use that training set alone. Bound
probabilities to [0.05, 0.95]. Logistic penalty is fixed at 10; nonlinear penalty
at 20; seed 20261117. Missing contextual inputs use training-set medians with
missingness flags. No model is promoted by its final-period result; report the
predeclared ensemble even if a baseline beats it.

## Scoring and uncertainty

Report sample count, direction accuracy, Brier score, log loss and calibration
bins for both labels. Compare paired Brier losses with the unconditional
baseline using 2,000 resamples of consecutive ten-session blocks. Include the
two halves of the evaluation period and high-confidence coverage. These are
conditional diagnostic intervals after an exploratory choice of models, not
confirmatory significance tests or a market-stationarity assumption.

Construct central 50% and 80% closing-return prediction intervals from the
preceding 252 resolved sessions' realized returns; compare with the 60 analogues'
empirical distribution. They are empirical forecast distributions, not confidence
intervals for the mean and not a guarantee that the intraday path stays inside.
Report walk-forward interval coverage. Session-high/low excursions are separate.

Dashboard options, international markets, flows and news can inform a written
scenario assessment. Without adequate timestamped historical coverage they do
not acquire invented fitted weights or an invented probability of success.
Correlated technical indicators and overlapping sectors are not independent votes.
For a 00:30 IST decision, a US daily bar for the previous calendar date may
still be in progress. Global history therefore requires its session date to
be strictly earlier than target date minus one calendar day. This conservative
daily convention discards partial US information instead of leaking its final close.

## Forward record

Save a timestamped, immutable forecast with the target date, reference close,
probabilities, intervals, raw-input hashes, model definition and unresolved
outcome fields. A later score command may write a separate outcome artifact;
it must not rewrite the original call. Do not use a scheduled automation.

# NIFTY session forecast experiment

The [17 November 2026 report](../../NIFTY_FORECAST_2026-11-17.md) records the
fixed forecast, all candidate results, current-factor scenarios and limitations.
The final artifact directory is `artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/run-v3`.
Earlier input attempts and output runs remain as research provenance; they are
not separate independent experiments. There was no parameter search between runs.

`PROTOCOL.md` defines the study. `collect.py` freezes read-only inputs;
`supplement.py` contains this date's additional global-history batch. `engine.py`
creates feature panels, monthly walk-forward replays and an immutable call.
`report.py` produces the readable report and static figure. `verify.py` checks
information boundaries; `score.py` resolves the call once the daily candle exists.
These modules do not submit orders or control bots.

Run from the repository root using `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m` followed by
the module name, for example `research.nifty_forecast.verify`. Reproduction must
use a new `--out` directory. The live collector is deliberately restricted to
the current pre-market date; saved input freezes support later reproduction.
The supplemental collector and report are specific to this dated experiment.

The model's weak historical performance is part of the recorded result.
The 59.8% raw upward output is not a demonstrated 59.8% success probability.

## Learned input weights

The [historical-error-weighted extension](../../NIFTY_LEARNED_WEIGHTS_2026-11-17.md)
learns 71 input coefficients inside 12 groups, then learns group allocations from
prior chronological prediction errors. Its final artifacts are in
`artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/adaptive-v2`; the first experiment remains
unchanged. `ADAPTIVE_PROTOCOL.md` specifies fitting, evidence gates and controls.

- `extend_history.py` retrieves overlapping read-only institutional windows.
- `adaptive.py` fits monthly experts, daily allocations and prior-only calibration.
- `adaptive_diagnostics.py` measures conditional weight stability and sensitivity.
- `adaptive_report.py` writes the report and research figure.
- `verify_adaptive.py` tests error learning and information boundaries.

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m research.nifty_forecast.verify_adaptive
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m research.nifty_forecast.adaptive --out artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/adaptive-reproduction-01
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m research.nifty_forecast.score --run artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/adaptive-v2
```

The last command remains pending until the official daily candle exists.
For a future session, supply fresh frozen paths through `--inputs`, `--supplement`,
`--institutional` and `--reference-run`, plus a new output directory. No automatic
watcher or scheduler runs. The learned forecast is neutral; the historical study
does not establish an edge. Calibration worsened this evaluation, and its result
remains disclosed rather than replaced after inspection.

## Strict two-year check

The [two-year rerun](../../NIFTY_TWO_YEAR_2026-11-17.md) restricts raw prices,
indicator initialization, fitting and error-learning history to 17 November 2024
through 16 November 2026. Outputs are in `artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/two-year-v1`.
Run `research.nifty_forecast.verify_two_year` for the boundary checks, or
`research.nifty_forecast.two_year --out <new-directory>` to reproduce it.
The 495-session total window leaves 96 decisions after training and weight-learning
warmup; it is not two years of independent out-of-sample forecasts.

## Week and month horizons

The [5/21-session experiment](../../NIFTY_WEEK_MONTH_2026-11-17.md) keeps the same
two-year input boundary but retrains separate weekly/monthly labels and weights.
Every training, weighting, calibration and magnitude outcome must have finished
its full horizon by the decision. `HORIZON_PROTOCOL.md` records the design.
Final artifacts are in `artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/horizons-v2`.

Run `research.nifty_forecast.verify_horizons` for ten focused checks and
`research.nifty_forecast.score_horizons --run artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/horizons-v2`
to score each horizon after maturity. No background watcher is running. The
monthly evaluation is poor and contains only two non-overlapping windows.

# Strict two-calendar-year rerun

User-directed restriction: only 17 November 2024 through 16 November 2026 may
contribute raw market observations, feature initialization, training labels,
prediction-error history, calibration or empirical return bands. Today's target
remains 17 November 2026. The first available Indian session is 18 November 2024.
Reuse the original dated input freeze; this isolates the history-window change.
Raw archived files contain earlier records, but clip every series before deriving
any feature. Do not import fitted states, coefficients, analogues or predictions
from a longer-history run.

Keep the existing 71-feature / 12-group method, penalties, recency half-lives,
252-row expert requirement, 126-prior-OOS evidence gate and monotone calibration.
The former 504-row overall startup holdoff cannot fit within a strict two-year
sample. Start expert predictions after 252 eligible feature rows, the existing
expert minimum. Rolling indicators consume their required observations inside
the window; EMAs and RSI initialize at its first observation. Monthly historical
refits and a fresh current fit remain unchanged.

Report all chronological predictions after initial expert training, then
separately report decisions with at least 126 resolved meta-training and
calibration examples. Select that evaluation by information availability, not
performance. Compare all fixed controls on the identical dates and disclose
their sample sizes. No claim of two full years of out-of-sample tests when the
same two years must also train the model. No hyperparameter search.

Recalculate current weights, coefficients, both directional estimates and the
trailing-252 empirical bands. Do not copy longer-history analogue statistics into
the new forecast. Preserve the earlier forecasts. Verify that changing values
before the boundary leaves the bounded features unchanged and that every fitted
training / calibration / meta label stays inside the window and precedes the
corresponding decision.

The data vintage, publication-clock assumptions, undated-options exclusions and
Monday provisional quote reconstruction remain as disclosed in the earlier
reports. This reused historical period is exploratory; today's outcome remains
unresolved.

# NIFTY forecast experiment — 17 November 2026

**Frozen call: a slight upward bias, with low confidence and substantial two-way risk.**
The fixed ensemble outputs **59.8% upward** for the close versus Monday's
25,291.10 reference, and **54.6% upward** from today's open to close.
These are raw model estimates, not demonstrated 60%/55% success rates.
The current US sell-off makes the domestic upward lean fragile. A clean bullish
trend throughout the session is not the forecast.

Issued **2026-11-17T00:41:57.880635+05:30**. Raw input batches were frozen at
2026-11-17T00:33:17.687726+05:30, 2026-11-17T00:34:15.755857+05:30. No 17 November Indian session prices
were available. Monday's quote is corroborated by the [NSE market page](https://www.nse.in/).
The [NSE 2026 holiday circular](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/circulars/CMTR71775.pdf)
and the saved Upstox holiday response show no scheduled holiday for 17 November.

## The actual call, ranges and ways it can fail

|Measure|Frozen estimate|Interpretation|
|---|---:|---|
|Close above Monday|59.8%|Raw ensemble probability; low trust in calibration|
|Close above today's open|54.6%|Separate outcome; models disagree materially|
|Analogue median close|25,311|About +20 points; a center estimate, not a precise target|
|Analogue weighted mean close|25,293|Almost flat; adverse tails offset frequent small gains|
|Central 50% historical closing band|25,173–25,429|Trailing 252-session empirical reference distribution|
|Central 80% historical closing band|25,008–25,559|An outside move remains possible|

The bands describe the **closing value**, not a boundary containing the intraday
path. Their walk-forward coverage was 45.6%
and 78.2%, respectively. They are deliberately
simple empirical bands rather than fitted precision targets.

Scenario markers, specified as a qualitative reading of observed levels:

- **Upward continuation:** acceptance above Monday's **25,337.60** high makes
  the recent **25,424.35** high the next reference; 25,500 is a nearby option-OI
  reference. These are conditional markers, not separately validated forecasts.
- **Two-way/base scenario:** repeated trading within Monday's **25,172.10–25,337.60**
  range would fit the weak directional evidence. The analogue median is 25,311.
- **Downward failure:** sustained trading below **25,172.10** would weaken the
  bullish reading; Friday's **25,054.40** low and the 25,000 area are lower references.
  Overnight news can gap directly through any of these levels.

## What the current inputs say

|Independent evidence group|Observed input at the freeze|Reading|
|---|---|---|
|Domestic prices|NIFTY +0.584%; Bank Nifty +0.888%; financials +0.574%|Supports an upward bias|
|Participation|31 advancing / 19 declining constituents, dated 15:29 IST; auto −1.288%, pharma −1.533%, metals −1.499%, realty −1.341%; FMCG +1.867%|Some breadth, but leadership is uneven and partly defensive|
|Overnight India proxy|GIFT Nifty 25,345.0, +0.196% versus its own previous value|Mild support; the futures/spot spread is not an exact opening-gap forecast|
|Global equities|S&P 500 -1.730%; Nasdaq -2.256%; Dow -1.230%; US futures -1.662%|The strongest contrary input; US cash session still open|
|Oil, currency and dollar|Brent 92.33, -3.662%; USD/INR 93.912, -0.130%; DXY +0.167%|Cheaper oil and firmer INR support India; global risk appetite is mixed|
|Volatility|India VIX 15.68, +1.161%|A move-size/risk input; not a directional vote|
|Participant futures|61,039 FII index-futures longs versus 117,726 shorts; net −56,687 contracts|Bearish positioning, which can also supply squeeze risk|
|Options and expiry|Listed expiry 17 November; PCR 0.944; max pain 25,200; ATM 25,300 straddle 167.9 points|Reference snapshot only: no publisher market timestamp|
|Cash institutions|FII/DII endpoint amounts fail the desk's documented-unit checks; official NSE adapter redirected|Excluded rather than assigning an unverified crore value|
|News and economic events|Upstox NIFTY news returned an empty object; no reliable complete event inventory was supplied|Unknown, not evidence that there are no events|

Current globals are delayed indicative quotes. The domestic constituent breadth
reading is near the close, not a separately verified closing breadth file.
Options OI does not reveal whether each position was initiated by a buyer or
writer. PCR, max pain and straddle premium have no fitted directional weight in
this experiment; straddle premium is not an 80% interval or a profit target.

## The historical check

The model uses **62 features**, **2,427 eligible feature rows**, Indian daily
history from January 2017, and available global history. Price features cover
returns, EMA distances, RSI, candle shape, gaps, realized volatility and ATR.
Context adds sector-relative returns, a sector participation proxy, India VIX,
and conservatively lagged completed global sessions. Sector participation is
not reconstructed constituent breadth; no present-day stock membership is
backfilled into a historical breadth label.

Fixed candidates and the equal-weight ensemble were specified in
[PROTOCOL.md](research/nifty_forecast/PROTOCOL.md) before performance was viewed.
The 504 target sessions run **4 November 2024–16 November 2026**. Each calendar
month is predicted with models fitted only to preceding resolved outcomes, with
at most 1,260 training examples. Scaling and imputation are fitted on training
data. Parameters were not tuned to this evaluation period.

|Model|Today's close-up estimate|Close accuracy|Close Brier ↓|Today's intraday-up estimate|Intraday accuracy|Intraday Brier ↓|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Historical frequency|52.1%|49.4%|0.2531|47.7%|52.8%|0.2497|
|Previous day|55.0%|52.8%|0.2497|55.0%|46.2%|0.2563|
|20-session trend|55.0%|50.8%|0.2517|55.0%|47.0%|0.2555|
|Price-only logistic|54.8%|53.2%|0.2529|43.5%|55.2%|0.2462|
|All-context logistic|54.5%|52.4%|0.2657|53.6%|51.0%|0.2554|
|60 historical analogues|57.5%|51.4%|0.2544|51.2%|52.2%|0.2503|
|Nonlinear random features|67.5%|51.4%|0.2573|58.8%|53.4%|0.2531|
|Fixed ensemble|59.8%|51.6%|0.2554|54.6%|52.8%|0.2497|
|Constant 50/50|50.0%|No directional call|0.2500|50.0%|No directional call|0.2500|

The main result is **no established predictive advantage from adding these
inputs**. The ensemble's close-direction accuracy is 51.6%, but its probability
score is worse than both historical frequency and constant 50/50. An always-down
direction would have been correct 50.6% of these sessions. The ensemble's paired
Brier improvement over historical frequency is −0.00229, with a conditional
95% ten-session-block interval of **-0.00928 to 0.00543**.
For intraday direction its accuracy matches the 52.8% frequency baseline; the
probability-score difference is negligible and its interval crosses zero.

Calibration is weak: close forecasts in the 55–60% bin occurred 105 times, but
only **48.6%** of those sessions closed up. Forecasts at least 60% upward occurred
156 times and closed up **55.8%** of the time. Today's 59.8% output therefore
cannot honestly be advertised as a calibrated 60% chance. The price-only model
currently gives only 43.5% for an up open-to-close session, versus 54.6% for the
ensemble. That disagreement is part of the result, not a reason to select a
different winner after the test.

The final replay observation uses Monday's provisional quote-derived daily
bar. A separate [503-session published-candle-only validation](artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/run-v3/validation-published-only.json)
excludes it. Its close ensemble Brier is
0.2554 versus
0.2532 for
the baseline, so the conclusion is unchanged.

## Data quality and coverage

The catalog now contains **127 concepts**, broader than the older 64-factor
research snapshot. The new freeze retains **46,757 dashboard observations**.
An observation count is not an independent daily sample count. The complete
[127-concept input audit](artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/run-v3/factor-inventory.md)
and its structured JSON preserve missing and excluded readings.

|Concept group|Total|Dated context|Undated context|Quality excluded|Unavailable|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|commodities currencies|9|9|0|0|0|
|derivatives options|15|0|12|0|3|
|earnings constituents|11|0|0|0|11|
|economy government|20|0|0|0|20|
|global markets|10|9|0|0|1|
|institutional flows|8|2|0|2|4|
|news events|13|0|0|0|13|
|rates bonds|8|1|0|0|7|
|sectors breadth|15|11|0|0|4|
|technicals|18|14|0|0|4|

"Dated context" means a timestamp exists; it does not certify freshness or
historical trainability. Factor JSON retains source dates and age. Raw historical
prices are today's revised history, not an archived point-in-time data vintage.
The following safeguards and limits matter:

- Upstox's NIFTY daily endpoint still stops at Friday, 13 November. 10 Monday
  Indian index/VIX bars are reconstructed from post-close quote OHLC; their
  previous close must match the published historical series. NIFTY 500's Monday
  context is missing and receives a training-derived imputation plus a flag.
- Auto history supplied 474 duplicate session rows, including 248 with differing
  OHLC values. Canonicalization deterministically prefers the midnight daily
  row; duplicates never become extra training samples.
- Global history contained **177 invalid OHLC rows**, rejected before features
  were built. Gaps are not silently turned into valid bars. Close changes between
  remaining observed sessions can span multiple calendar days.
- For a 00:30 IST decision, the preceding US cash day may still be open. Fitted
  global features require a source date strictly earlier than target date minus
  one calendar day. This is conservative for Asian markets. The ongoing US
  sell-off appears in the written scenarios, not retrospectively in the fitted
  feature panel. The model therefore omits useful information visible now.
- Price, flow and option history do not have the same coverage. Recent snapshots
  were not backfilled across years; cash amounts with uncertain units were not used.
- [Upstox documents](https://upstox.com/developer/api-documentation/v3/get-historical-candle-data/)
  a maximum decade per daily request; the successful batch uses January 2017
  onward. Source errors and both acquisition and market times are preserved.

## Reproduce and score

Seven focused checks pass: raw-input hashes, unfinished-US-day exclusion,
invariance to future Indian-price changes, training-only scaling, next-session
labels, chronological walk-forward training, and logistic probability sanity.

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m research.nifty_forecast.verify
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m research.nifty_forecast.engine --out artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/reproduction-01
```

After the target session closes and Upstox publishes its daily candle:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m research.nifty_forecast.score
```

The scorer writes a separate outcome file with the official daily open/close,
reference revisions, direction outcomes, Brier scores and interval hits. It
leaves the original [forecast.json](artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/run-v3/forecast.json)
unchanged. The outcome is currently **unresolved**. No scheduler or orders were
created, and no existing bot configuration was changed.

The statistical experiment and the qualitative scenario assessment are both
frozen here. A better experiment from this starting point is a series of future
calls at one fixed clock, with timestamped intraday global inputs and published
option/flow observations captured prospectively. One good or bad day will not
establish whether the method works.

# NIFTY inputs weighted by historical prediction errors

**The learned-weight call for 17 November 2026 is neutral.** The primary estimate
is **49.75%** for a close above the preceding close and **49.45%** for
a close above today's open. This replaces the bullish interpretation of the
first experiment for this new version; the original timestamped 59.8% call is

## How the machine assigns weights

The design is recorded in [ADAPTIVE_PROTOCOL.md](research/nifty_forecast/ADAPTIVE_PROTOCOL.md).
There are **71 raw features in 12 disjoint groups**. The feature and group layers
have different jobs:

1. **Learn each input's signed coefficient.** Every group has an L2 logistic
   expert. Monthly fits use only already resolved sessions, up to 1,260 rows,
   with a 252-session recency half-life and fixed penalty 25. Normalization and
   missing-value handling use only its own training data. Missingness has its
   own coefficients.
2. **Make historical predictions before seeing their answers.** For example, a
   prediction for session D uses only resolved targets before D. The actual D
   result becomes eligible for changing the next session's blend, not D's own
   forecast. Monthly experts stay frozen within their month; the current forward
   call receives a fresh fit with all outcomes now resolved.
3. **Learn group trust from those errors.** Before each decision, choose
   nonnegative weights summing to one to minimize Brier loss on up to the prior
   504 out-of-sample forecasts. Recent errors have a 126-session half-life. A
   fixed 0.005 squared penalty favors the neutral expert when evidence is weak.
   This joint fit accounts for overlap between experts rather than counting
   correlated indicators as independent votes.
4. **Fit calibration to previous forecasts.** A monotone logistic mapping learns
   from at most 252 preceding adaptive forecasts, with at least 126 required.
   It has penalty 10 toward no adjustment. Calibration is evaluated as a
   separate layer; it is not assumed to improve every test period.

No weights are chosen from the entire evaluation period and then applied back
to its beginning. Group allocations change daily as earlier results resolve.
[Daily weights](artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/adaptive-v2/daily-weights-close_return.csv),
[historical expert predictions](artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/adaptive-v2/expert-predictions-close_return.csv)
and the dated expert-fit files make that sequence inspectable.

## Institutional history: more data, carefully used

The [Upstox FII documentation](https://upstox.com/developer/api-documentation/get-fii-data/)
states that collection begins on 1 April 2026 and daily requests return at most
30 trading days. Overlapping requests and the saved current window recovered
**156 unique source sessions**, 1 April–16 November,
with **155 aligned training rows** and no conflicting duplicate revisions.
Returned session timestamps, rather than the misleading request parameter name,
govern the join. One source date does not align to the NIFTY daily calendar.

The cash features are **(buy − sell)/(buy + sell)**, including five-session
averages. A common INR/crore scale cancels exactly; absolute crore values remain
unverified. Negative amounts, invalid values and a zero denominator are rejected.
Futures features use long/short and trade-contract imbalances; participant option
positioning uses normalized long-call/short-put versus long-put/short-call
exposure. That last measure is a contract-count proxy, not a delta-weighted book.

These experts have **73 genuine historical OOS predictions**
after their initial training requirement. The primary blend requires 126 such
predictions and 252 training rows. They therefore receive **0% primary weight**
and are retained in shadow, where their predictions and coefficients can be
scored as additional history arrives. Their current close-up estimates of
64.4% and 63.0% do not bypass that gate.

Institutional EOD values are assumed published before the next 00:30 IST
decision. The API's session timestamp does not prove a publication clock, so
this is reconstructed history rather than an archived publication-vintage replay.
Unknown-time chain PCR, IV, max pain, and unarchived macro/news concepts likewise
have no fitted primary weight; no synthetic years of observations were created.

## Did learning weights improve the predictions?

The evaluation contains **504 sessions, 4 November 2024–16 November 2026**.
The latest 126 and both chronological halves are reported in JSON. This period
was already examined in the first study, so it is an **exploratory reused
evaluation**, not an untouched confirmation set. Its individual forecasts still
obey historical information boundaries. The next actual session remains forward.

|Method|Close Brier ↓|Close accuracy|Intraday Brier ↓|Intraday accuracy|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Neutral 50/50|0.25000|—|0.25000|—|
|Daily rolling frequency|0.25289|49.4%|0.24976|52.8%|
|Equal eligible groups|0.25115|48.8%|0.24816|55.4%|
|Learned group weights|0.25025|52.8%|0.24971|50.8%|
|Learned weights + calibration (primary)|0.25232|49.6%|0.25090|51.0%|
|Original fixed ensemble|0.25541|51.6%|0.24970|52.8%|

The raw learned blend improves close Brier loss from the first ensemble's
0.25541 to **0.25025** and scores **52.8%** direction
accuracy. It remains essentially tied with the neutral 0.25000 reference. Its
paired improvement against neutral is -0.00025,
with conditional 95% block interval **-0.00281 to +0.00284**.

The predeclared primary calibrated model scores **0.25232** and
**49.6%** close accuracy. Its improvement versus neutral is
-0.00232, interval **-0.00545 to +0.00145**.
**Calibration made this evaluation worse.** It is retained and disclosed as
specified, rather than replacing the primary method with whichever control won
after seeing the results. Intraday learned weighting and calibration also fail
to establish an advantage over the controls. The equal-group intraday control
has a better point estimate, with its uncertainty interval still crossing zero.

Thus weights have been learned and changed the forecast, but a reliable
directional edge has **not** been established. Improvement from an overconfident
first model is not the same as beating a neutral forecast. A separate
[503-session check](artifacts/nifty_forecast/2026-11-17/adaptive-v2/validation.json)
excludes Monday's provisional quote-derived target and reaches the same broad
conclusion. Both raw and calibrated estimates are frozen; a 49.7% estimate is
operationally neutral, not a high-confidence bearish call.

A diagnostic 300-resample, ten-session-block bootstrap refits the current stack

These are conditional weight-stability diagnostics, not confidence bounds for
universal economic importance. The regularization and selected feature groups
remain fixed; historical stationarity is not guaranteed.

## Outcome maturity and move-size estimation

For an origin after session t's close, the return is **C[t+h]/C[t] − 1**. An
earlier forecast may teach the model only after its endpoint has closed.
Yesterday's monthly forecast is still unresolved today. This restriction applies
to expert fitting, group-weight learning, calibration and magnitude history.

The earlier fixed penalties, feature groups and recency half-lives are retained.
Historical experts refit monthly; the current call gets a fresh fit. The first
expert forecast waits for 252 matured training labels, and primary weighting and
calibration each need 126 matured OOS errors. No parameter grid was searched.
The [fixed design](research/nifty_forecast/HORIZON_PROTOCOL.md) and dated fits record this.

Move sizes use up to 252 matured returns at the appropriate horizon. Positive
and nonpositive historical sizes receive total mass p and 1−p from the fitted
upward estimate. This assumes historical conditional sizes persist. It is not
a separately fitted price regressor. Quantiles use an empirical inverse CDF;
no unfinished weekly/monthly return enters the distribution.
